findings.evidence: “It is the only zero-external-dependency option” and “only its position in its role's order decides priority” repeat the rationale and fallback rule in the mandatory session-default reference.
findings.fix: Keep the always-ask instruction and the explicit purpose requirement at Step 2.7. Consolidate the priority rationale and last-place fallback guidance in references/session-default.md, where that step already sends the reader.

findings.evidence: “Skip this section unless a preferred runtime has no listing” requires a choice the owner has not made at Step 1.5. The preferred-runtime questions first occur in wizard-flow.md step 1, and its next step does not route back to the optional sources.
findings.fix: Keep initial catalog discovery in Step 1.5. Route to the optional-source section from wizard-flow.md step 2, after the owner picks preferred runtimes and before candidate reconciliation. Carry forward any no-fetch decision and require separate consent for a pane launch.

findings.evidence: “Detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set from the model catalog for the owner to pick, asks each role's order, effort and opt-in flags” spends much of the 1,013-character description on the wizard's mechanics before reaching its triggers.
findings.fix: Use when setting up, refreshing, or checking ai-kit's cross-AI reviewers and implementers, even if the user does not say “lanes” or a review or execute run reports that no lanes exist. Choose models and per-role fallbacks, then save [lanes] in .aikit/config.toml or the user config. --local and --global select the file, not permission to replace it. Use --check-only for availability without config writes. Also use to check stale OpenCode lane providers or diagnose pending review-spec.toml migration. Not for running configured lanes, hand-editing one lane setting, or changing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: The always-loaded workflow includes the full “When this prints {"vendor": null}” decision tree, even though it applies only when attribution fails. The 426-line body has about 6,500 words and exceeds the recommended 5,000-token instruction layer despite its existing conditional references.
findings.fix: Keep the exact infer-vendor call and a direct conditional link in Step 2.3. Put the null-result choices and their single/double routing consequences in a focused references/vendor-attribution.md, loaded only on a null result. Use the same pattern for other long exception branches while keeping consent and validation gates inline.

findings.evidence: “A change made between that read and the write is not caught.” The agent's separate reread cannot enforce that --replace applies only to the roster the owner approved.
findings.fix: Have render-toml check an expected roster digest under its existing folder lock before migration or replacement. On mismatch, write nothing and return to the replacement question with the newly observed roster.

findings.evidence: “On a declined test, runs no check-reviewer call and reports the entry as untested” can pass even if the entry was never written; the expected result at line 88 explicitly requires saving it.
findings.fix: Use a synthetic runtime listing and target config in this case. Assert that the chosen entry exists in parsed output TOML, no check-reviewer call ran, and the report names that same key as untested.

findings.evidence: “Which providers does my opencode review config reference that are no longer listed?” repeats the stale-provider intent at line 6. The set has 12 positives and 10 negatives, but lacks a direct contrast between checking ai-kit lane availability and listing models in OpenCode itself.
findings.fix: Keep one stale-lane-provider positive and replace the duplicate with a paired near-miss: a user asking only to list selectable models in OpenCode, without inspecting or changing ai-kit lanes.

findings.evidence: “Write no config, cache or trust record” is too broad for the headless path. detect-runtimes invokes OpenCode through detection.py's _private_dir, which can create the cache base; Cursor model enumeration can rewrite its own privacy cache. Both happen before the headless stop or check-only consent prompt.
findings.fix: Distinguish 'no ai-kit roster, snapshot, catalog or trust write' from 'no filesystem changes.' For headless or strict no-change requests, use binary-presence-only detection before consent and report model counts as unknown unless the owner permits live enumeration.

findings.evidence: “Confirm the trusted bytes are the approved ones” compares only key and argv (or error) for rendered entries. The trust digest also includes fields such as vendor that need not affect argv, so a changed entry can be trusted without triggering revocation.
findings.fix: Have the preview return the canonical command-bearing roster digest alongside the invocation and field display. Require the trusting form to match that approved digest before recording trust, and repeat the preview and consent if it differs.

findings.evidence: The effort-probe command ends at “--effort <level>” even though the preceding step already chose the lane's knobs. A codex lane with a selected service tier tests effort without that tier, then saves acceptance evidence for the configured lane. The probe implementation uses the extra fields supplied to it; it does not recover omitted knobs.
findings.fix: Pass the selected non-effort knobs via --extra-json in the effort probe as well as the pair probe. Keep --catalog-path off the effort probe, and describe what was tested as the review invocation with those settings.

findings.evidence: The write example uses “--out <target path>” while quoting the scratch and runtimes paths. After literal substitution, a valid project or user path containing spaces is split into multiple shell arguments.
findings.fix: Show --out "<target path>" and --catalog-path "<catalog>" in the write example, with a note to pass each recorded path as one shell-escaped argument.
